title: EESD yield-adaptive in-QP MPC: online tangent-stiffness model-updating vs the fixed-model in-QP deep-yield failure (multi-height)
hypothesis: Updating the in-QP MPC's internal prediction model to the current tangent stiffness (estimated online from measured inter-story drift) REMOVES the 3-story fixed-model deep-yield failure and gives a robust positive margin across heights -- softening info is useful for MODEL-UPDATING, not gain-retuning.
adaptive_model: K_tan(beta)=K0+sum_s (beta_s-1) k_s e_s e_s'; beta_s from inter-story drift ductility via secant->tangent map; rate-limited + event-triggered re-form.
honesty_scope: Validated BILINEAR plant; drift/accel only. clip-LQR, fixed-elastic in-QP, fixed-softened in-QP baselines share U_MAX, horizon, weights, state, records.

summary_lines: [3-story] fixed-model in-QP fails (loses to clip) in 3 case(s); on those, adaptive cuts J over the fixed model by +0.155 on average (e.g. the worst case northrdg x1.0: 1.003->0.632, removing ~90% of the +0.411 failure gap) but only fully crosses the clip baseline in 0/3 (adaptive lands just ABOVE clip on the rest).
[3-story deep-yield] mean J: clip=0.806 fixed=0.736 ADAPT=0.822 | adapt-vs-clip=+0.017 adapt-vs-fixed=+0.087 (adapt beats clip 1/5, beats fixed 1/5)
[9-story deep-yield] mean J: clip=0.883 fixed=0.808 ADAPT=0.961 | adapt-vs-fixed=+0.153 adapt-vs-clip=+0.078 unstable=0 chatter=0.000
VERDICT.overall: NULL / NOT MULTI-HEIGHT-ROBUST: online model-updating SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCES the worst 3-story deep-yield failures (cuts fixed-model J by ~0.15-0.23 on the fail cases, removing ~90% of the worst gap and turning a +0.41 loss into a +0.04 near-tie with clip) and is net-positive vs the fixed model on the 3-story CANONICAL set (-0.046). BUT it does NOT cleanly cross the clipped-LQR baseline, and it REVERSES into a net LOSS at extreme deep-yield (3-story deep adapt-vs-fixed +0.087) and UNIFORMLY HURTS the 9-story (deep adapt-vs-fixed +0.153) where the fixed model already wins; the harm is clean OVER-SOFTENING, not numerical breakdown (no instability, negligible beta-chatter) -- softening the internal model degrades the in-QP controller whenever the elastic model was NOT actually mispredicting (extreme deep-yield where clipping already dominates, and the 9-story where the fixed model already wins). NET across cases/heights it is a wash-to-negative vs the fixed in-QP. => The softening-info-for-model-updating angle is NOT a clean robust positive; EESD's positive contribution stays thin -- prefer A-modest or B. (Of note: the static global-softening cell -- fixed alpha*K0, no online adaptation -- is the more robust single choice, and a monotone-ratchet adaptive matches the failure-repair at near-zero re-form cost; both are honest sub-findings but neither flips the multi-height verdict.)
